newsitem.title: USA: Ma. nanny case prosecutors refuse comment on charges.
newsitem.headline: Ma. nanny case prosecutors refuse comment on charges.

text.p: Prosecutors on Friday declined to say in court how they would prove that a British au pair wilfully killed a baby left in her charge.
Louise Woodward, 19, of Chester, England, is accused of killing 9-month-old Matthew Eappen, who was left in her charge at the Eappen family home in Newton, Massachusetts in early February.

Prosecutors have charged Woodward with first-degree murder in the death and therefore must be prepared to prove she knowingly and wilfully and with premeditation killed the baby. A jury is expected to hear the case in July and could return guilty verdicts on that or on lesser charges.

When Middlesex County Superior Court Judge Hiller Zobel asked prosecutor Lynn Rooney if she was prepared to discuss the first-degree murder charge and how she would prove premeditation, Rooney replied, "I'd prefer not to do that at this time."
The judge advised her to "expect to be called on to do it (discuss proving premeditation) on or before May 30," when he set another date for a court hearing.
The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court will hear Woodward's lawyer, Andrew Good, argue on Wednesday that his client should be freed on bail.

Zobel denied bail to the teenager, although she presented numerous affidavits attesting to her good character and background in an effort to win her release. She has been kept without bail at the state's women-only prison facility since her arrest in mid-February.
